subject: Re: Aperture AI — escrowed prepay & staggered capacity plan
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@aperture.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — multi-year ramp ask

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Aperture is interested in a multi-year Dedicated contract but we need a phased GPU ramp to match product milestones. High-level ask: start with a small pilot (8 A100-equivalent GPUs) in Q4, double in Q1, and reach 48 GPUs by month 10. We would prefer an annual prepay structure but need an escrow mechanism or milestone-based release because we cannot fully prepay for the entire term up front.

Key questions for pricing:
- What term discounts do you offer for 24-36 month commitments?
- Can you bind discounts to committed peak capacity while allowing staged provisioning?
- How do you treat refunds or credits if we miss ramp milestones?

We have procurement and legal on copy — would like a sketch number and a short payment+milestone proposal to run internally.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Infrastructure
Aperture AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@aperture.ai>
Cc: procurement@aperture.ai, legal@aperture.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — multi-year ramp ask

Samir — thanks for the clear brief. High level: we can do an annual prepay with an escrow-release schedule tied to milestones. Attached is a simple ramp worksheet + term summary (Aperture_Ramp_Schedule_v1.xlsx, Redwood_Dedicated_Term_Summary.pdf).

Quick sketch (illustrative):
- Term: 24 months (option to convert to 36 at +3% rate lock)
- Committed peak: 48 GPUs (A100-equivalent)
- Pricing: base unit price $X per GPU-hour, with tiered term discount: 10% at 12mo, 16% at 24mo, 20% at 36mo on list hosted rates.
- Prepay: Aperture prepays 60% of year-1 and 40% of year-2 into an escrow account managed by a third-party custodian. Funds are released against milestones (pilot live, Q1 scale, production readiness) — see attached schedule.
- Milestone credits: if a ramp milestone is missed by more than 30 days and not due to force majeure, Redwood issues a pro-rated credit against future months (up to 3% of the prepaid tranche for the missed milestone).

We can provide an amortization example (how prepay maps to monthly usage credits) and a DocuSign-ready term summary if this matches your expectations. I'm copying our finance lead Laura and sales lead Karthik to validate the finance mechanics and discount stack.

Would you like us to draft the escrow instructions and a milestone checklist for your procurement/legal to review?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@aperture.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aperture.ai, legal@aperture.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — multi-year ramp ask

Thanks Marissa — the sketch looks promising. A couple of clarifying items before we loop legal: 

1) Escrow custodian — can Redwood propose the custodian or do we need to nominate one? We prefer a neutral third-party.
2) Milestone timing — our product milestones are strict: pilot (30 days), scale to 24 GPUs (90 days), peak (month 10). Can the release schedule be aligned to those exact check-in dates?
3) Credits/penalties — instead of pro-rated credit, can we do milestone release holdback (e.g., 10% of tranche held until final ramp), and if milestone fails, that holdback converts to extension credit for the term? That helps our CFO with cash flow planning.

Also, please confirm whether committed peak is billed if we don't consume it (we'd like committed minimum billing to be applied only after the scheduled ramp month).

If you can send a revised schedule + a simple example amortization table for a 24-month prepay with 60/40 split, that will help accelerate internal approval.

—Samir

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@aperture.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, procurement@aperture.ai, legal@aperture.ai
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — multi-year ramp ask

Samir — looping in Karthik (sales lead) and Laura (finance). We can support the holdback model you described — that's workable and simpler to operate than proportional credits. Summary of updated mechanics below (I also attached an updated schedule in the Drive link):

Updated proposal (24-month, illustrative numbers left as $X for commercial discussion):
- Prepay split: 60% Year-1 up front (Escrow deposit A), 40% Year-2 released to Redwood but subject to 6-months notice and amortization.
- Escrow mechanics: third-party custodian (we can propose a recommended custodian; final selection by mutual agreement). Escrow releases: 30% of Escrow deposit A released on pilot go-live; 40% released on 24-GPU scale checkpoint; remaining 30% held as final ramp holdback and released at month 10 on verified peak.
- Holdback fallback: if a milestone is missed >30 days and not cured within 45 days, remaining holdback converts to a term credit applied evenly across the remainder of the 24-month term (not refunded).
- Billing treatment: committed peak is not billed until its scheduled month; we apply minimum billing only for capacity that has passed its ramp month. Unused committed capacity before the scheduled month is not invoiced.
- Discounts: 16% term discount for 24 months; addendum to convert to 36 months at +3% list adjustment and 20% discount.

Action items:
- Karthik: can you confirm the discount ladder and example $ numbers we should show in the amortization table?
- Laura: can you confirm the escrow release language we typically use and whether the holdback -> term credit flow needs extra compliance review?
- Samir: confirm custodian preference and whether procurement needs a separate SOW for the milestone verification step.

If that aligns, I'll prepare a short term summary and a DocuSign envelope for signature-ready commercial terms and the escrow instruction template.

Thanks — Marissa
